layer1_evidence.interpretation_en: A 60-year-old woman has an approximately 2 cm hard, poorly mobile right breast mass, with hypertension and Hashimoto thyroiditis; this supports further diagnostic and treatment evaluation but does not alone establish malignancy or stage.

The right breast mass at approximately 11 o'clock was BI-RADS 5 on both ultrasound and mammography, with localization completed, strongly suggesting malignancy. No obvious enlarged axillary or supraclavicular nodes were seen, which does not exclude nodal metastasis.

Core biopsy of the right breast mass at 11 o'clock indicates carcinoma with mucin secretion. This provides histologic evidence of carcinoma, while immunohistochemistry remains in progress and receptor status and complete classification are not yet finalized.

management_state.canonical_en: Continue inpatient postoperative recovery, flap and drainage management, await pathology results, and subsequently arrange oncology specialty follow-up and adjuvant-treatment assessment.

required_delta_from_previous_checkpoint.canonical_en: New postoperative recovery documentation shows stable vital signs and a well-approximated incision, with continued skin-flap and drain monitoring and rehabilitation guidance required.
The management state has advanced to inpatient postoperative recovery, with chest-wall and axillary drains still in place.

treatment_readiness.canonical_en: Definitive surgery has been completed, and conditions are currently present to continue standard postoperative monitoring and recovery management; conditions are not yet present to formulate a complete subsequent tumor-treatment plan based on final pathology.

hard_failure_rules_en: Misreporting a negative frozen sentinel lymph node as final lymph-node negativity or a complete staging conclusion.
Determine a specific adjuvant treatment regimen based on speculation when immunohistochemistry and final pathology are not complete.
Disregard postoperative flap, incision, or drainage monitoring, or directly determine safe discharge without assessing recovery.
critical_omission_rules_en: Immunohistochemistry and final pathology result tracking have not been arranged.
No drain care, drain-removal assessment, or postoperative rehabilitation guidance was provided.

stopping.rationale_en: Postoperative vital signs are stable and the incision is well approximated, but drains and ongoing postoperative management remain necessary. Immunohistochemistry and final pathology will affect characterization, staging, and subsequent treatment. Therefore, treatment should continue rather than stopping or moving directly to routine follow-up.
remaining_blockers_en: Postoperative flap, incision, chest wall, and axillary drainage still require continuous monitoring.
Immunohistochemistry and final surgical pathology have not yet been completed.
Extubation and discharge criteria still need to be assessed according to recovery status.

question.question_en: At this time point, use only available evidence to identify key evidence, supported claims, patient state, appropriate next actions, and whether stopping or follow-up is safe.

completion_criteria_en: Breast malignancy has been confirmed by pathology, and final pathology and necessary immunohistochemical classification have been completed.
partial_criteria_en: Core-needle biopsy has confirmed right breast cancer, but immunohistochemistry or final surgical pathology has not yet been completed.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Final pathology is inconsistent with the existing diagnosis, or specimen quality is insufficient to support the diagnosis.

completion_criteria_en: Final pathology, lymph node pathology, and necessary immunohistochemistry information have been obtained, and staging and subsequent treatment assessment have been completed on this basis.
partial_criteria_en: Definitive surgery and sentinel lymph node frozen assessment have been completed, but final pathology and immunohistochemistry are still pending.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Key pathology or staging materials are missing, specimens are unreliable, or the patient's condition does not permit the planned treatment.

completion_criteria_en: The planned right simple mastectomy, sentinel lymph-node biopsy, and lymph-node management performed according to intraoperative findings have been completed.
partial_criteria_en: Mastectomy and sentinel lymph node surgery have been completed, but postoperative pathology or the scope of planned treatment still requires final review.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Postoperatively, it is found that surgery was not completed, that surgical complications requiring immediate management are present, or that additional emergency surgery is required.

completion_criteria_en: The incision and flap are stable, drainage management has been completed or tube-removal criteria have been met, rehabilitation guidance has been provided, and the postoperative care plan has been completed.
partial_criteria_en: Postoperative vital signs are stable and the incision is well approximated, but the flap, drainage volume, and functional recovery still need monitoring.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Occurrence of flap ischemia, active bleeding, infection, abnormal drainage, or other conditions requiring escalation of management.

completion_criteria_en: Meet safe discharge criteria, complete drain and wound care education, and implement pathology result tracking, breast surgery follow-up, and oncology specialty follow-up.
partial_criteria_en: Needed specialist follow-up and pathology-result tracking have been identified, but the patient remains hospitalized and the drain is in place; discharge conditions have not yet been completed.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Continuity of drainage care, pathology-result follow-up, or necessary specialist follow-up could not be ensured.

normalized_evidence.content_summary: A 60-year-old woman noticed a right breast mass approximately 3 weeks ago, measuring approximately 2 cm, hard in consistency, and with poor mobility, and was admitted for further diagnosis and treatment; comorbid hypertension and Hashimoto thyroiditis.
